who: Whitman H. Ridgway, historian at the University of Maryland, College Park.

evidence.says: Lists Whitman H. Ridgway as associate professor emeritus of history, with research on the early American republic.
The authority cites The Bill of Rights (1992), identifying Whitman H. Ridgway with the University of Maryland, College Park.

notes: The authority record explicitly supplies the students’ university and the supervisor’s full name.

who: Donald Rowland, Latin American historian at the University of Southern California, with a Berkeley doctorate.

evidence.says: A 1947 review by Donald Rowland gives his affiliation as the University of Southern California.
In his university oral history, Rudy Acuña recalls studying at USC and describes Donald Rowland as a Berkeley PhD who studied under Bolton.
Donald Trevor Rowland is identified as a reader in population studies at the Australian National University and author of Demographic Methods and Concepts.
The Donald F. Rowland authority cites Lawyers, Courts, and Deprived Children, without an institutional affiliation or degree.

notes: The USC supervisor is identifiable, but none of the supplied authorities could be connected securely to him. Some candidates are clearly different authors; sparse records, especially Donald F. Rowland, prevent excluding every candidate.

who: Gustav L. Seligmann, University of North Texas historian; PhD Arizona, 1967.

evidence.says: Gustav L. Seligmann joined UNT in 1967, earned his Arizona PhD that year, and co-edited The Sweep of American History.
The authority for Gustav L. Seligmann cites The Sweep of American History (1969–).

notes: University, doctorate and year match the AHA context; the university page also connects him to the authority’s cited work.

who: Carl Edward Skeen, historian at Memphis State University / University of Memphis; PhD Ohio State, 1966.

evidence.says: The 1996–97 Memphis faculty catalogue lists Carl Edward Skeen in history, appointed in 1968, with an Ohio State PhD in 1966.
Carl Edward Skeen has the variant name C. Edward Skeen; the record cites John Armstrong, Jr., 1758–1843 and 1816.

notes: The expanded name, institution and doctorate match; LC explicitly records the form used by AHA.

who: Barbara Welter, American historian at Hunter College and the CUNY Graduate Center; PhD Wisconsin.

evidence.says: Lists Barbara Welter as emeritus faculty in American history, affiliated with Hunter College, with a Wisconsin PhD and publications on American women.
The authority cites her The Woman Question in American Politics (1973), identifying an author in the relevant American-history field.
The other Barbara Welter authority is established from Modedesign Schweiz (1997).

notes: The CUNY affiliation, Wisconsin doctorate and American women’s history distinguish the supervisor from the fashion-history candidate.

who: Charles Wetzel, history professor at Drew University.

evidence.says: The university newspaper identifies Charles Wetzel as professor of history and leader of Drew’s Bicentennial Committee.
The Charles Wetzel authority cites James Monroe (1989), but gives no affiliation or doctorate.
The Charles Robert Wetzel authority records the publication name C. Robert Wetzel and cites Essays on New Testament Christianity.

notes: n87920145 is plausible by subject, but no source found connects the James Monroe author to Drew or the Wisconsin doctorate. The name alone is insufficient.

who: Roger Wines, Fordham historian of modern Germany; PhD Columbia.

evidence.says: Identifies Roger Wines as professor emeritus of history and gives a Columbia PhD, dated 1959; lists work on European and German history.
Lists Roger Wines in the history faculty, with Columbia doctorate and specialties in modern Germany and New York history and archaeology.
The Roger Wines authority includes the affiliation Fordham University.

notes: LC directly supplies the matching institution. Fordham dates the PhD to 1959, whereas AHA records 1961; the year discrepancy remains unresolved.

who: Winthrop R. Wright, Latin American historian at the University of Maryland, College Park.

evidence.says: The publisher identifies Café con leche author Winthrop R. Wright as professor of history at Maryland, College Park.
The 1974–75 award record identifies Winthrop Wright as an assistant professor of history at Maryland, College Park.
The Winthrop R. Wright authority cites Café con leche and gives the expanded name Winthrop Robins Wright, Jr.

notes: The authority’s cited book connects its author explicitly to the students’ institution; the Fulbright record confirms the relevant period.
